processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloys were made of high-purity elements: Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.99%), Al (99.99%), C (99.99%) and Be (99.99%), melted into alloy ingots; ingot diameter 60 mm and thickness 30 mm. Nominal composition Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–1.0Be (wt%).

processing_steps.method: as-cast (no heat treatment, no thermal deformation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: As-cast terminal state: the ingot was left as-cast; no heat treatment and no thermal deformation were applied (as-cast Fe–Mn–Al–C system steel without heat treatment and thermal deformation cannot obtain a uniform microstructure).

structures.overall_structure: Dual-phase austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) with Be–Fe compound precipitates (as-cast); ferrite is evenly distributed in the austenite matrix and the Be–Fe phase is randomly distributed
structures.number_of_phases: 3 (austenite γ + ferrite δ + Be–Fe compound precipitates)

phases_present.morphology: large bright blocky/vermiform islands embedded in the austenite matrix
randomly distributed dark point-like/needle-like/rod-like precipitates and 'ancient Chinese character' shaped precipitates; dark inter-island regions in OM

precipitates.distribution: randomly distributed in the as-cast microstructure; associated with ferrite/austenite regions
randomly distributed in the as-cast microstructure
randomly distributed in the as-cast microstructure

interfaces.phase_evolution: With increasing Be content the as-cast microstructure changes from a single austenite (0Be, 0.5Be) to a γ + δ dual-phase structure accompanied by Be–Fe compound precipitates (1.0Be, 1.5Be); the addition of Be promotes the formation of the ferrite phase.
interfaces.interface_notes: In the as-cast 1.0Be structure the Be–Fe compound precipitates (ancient Chinese-character shaped) appear at the boundary between austenite and ferrite and are widely distributed (b0074); the Be–Fe phase is randomly distributed and ferrite is evenly distributed in the austenite matrix (b0028).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness; load 500 gf; each sample tested with a 15×5 matrix and the average of 25 points taken as the microhardness value; measured with FM-ARS9000 Vickers hardness tester

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: X-ray diffractometer with Cu Kα X-ray tube (D/MAX-2500/PC, ASTM: D5380–93[2014])
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 2θ range 20°–100°, scanning speed 2° per min, continuous scanning; specimen polished with #150–#800 waterproof sandpaper and ultrasonically cleaned with alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the phase composition of as-cast Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steels
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 1.0Be: phase composition is austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) + partial precipitates; the ferrite (110) diffraction intensity increased (2θ = 44.67°), indicating Be promotes ferrite formation; Be2Fe and Be12Fe peaks appear around the Be11Fe peaks (Fig. 1)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Axiovert 200 MAT optical microscope; etched with 8% nitrate alcohol solution; surface finish 0.05 µm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Polished with #400–#5000 waterproof sandpapers followed by 0.5 µm diamond suspension; 50 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the as-cast microstructure of the Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steels
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 1.0Be (Fig. 2c): clearly dual-phase structure with large bright blocky/vermiform δ islands in a darker γ matrix and dark inter-island regions labelled 'Beryllium compound' (50 µm scale bar)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FM-ARS9000 Vickers hardness tester; 500 gf load; 15×5 matrix; average of 25 points
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Matrix (austenite), ferrite and Be–Fe phase measured separately on the as-cast steel
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the microhardness of the as-cast matrix (austenite), ferrite and Be–Fe phase
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 1.0Be: austenite 475.80 ±13.75 HV, ferrite 437.40 ±15.72 HV, Be–Fe phase 483.50 ±16.65 HV; hardness (of austenite) of the as-cast matrix increases with Be content

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens prepared by standard metallographic methods (up to #5000 sandpaper and 0.5 µm diamond polishing) and etched in 8% nitrate alcohol solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the microstructure of the alloys (including as-cast states)

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) bright-field imaging and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM foil thinned to 40 µm with waterproof sandpaper, then dual-jet electrochemical polishing in 10% perchloric acid + 90% ethanol at 26.5 V and −20 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the morphology of the Be–Fe phase precipitates in as-cast steels
characterization_methods.key_findings: In as-cast 0.5Be steel the Be–Fe (Be12Fe) precipitates measure 5–10 µm and were identified along the [−113] and [001] zone axes; in as-cast 1.5Be steel large Be12Fe precipitates intersect perpendicularly and an AlFe3 pattern ([011]) was indexed

unmapped_findings: Density of the 1.0Be steel is reported as 6.36 ±0.04 g/cm³ (Table 3); however Table 3 is captioned 'Tensile experiment of rolling (1050 °C) Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steels' and the density column is presented alongside the rolling-state values, so its state attribution relative to the as-cast sample is ambiguous (block b0065, b0099).

DSC measurement of the 1.0Be alloy (heating after homogenisation) gives a phase-transformation peak at 1163.3 °C (Fig. 6); the text states the 1.0Be transformation temperature decreased by approximately 1 °C relative to 0.5Be. This DSC was recorded after homogenisation, not on the as-cast state (block b0035, figure_006).

A calculated equilibrium Fe–Be binary phase diagram (Fig. 19) is presented, showing stoichiometric line compounds FeBe12 (~0.13), FeBe5 (~0.17) and FeBe2 (~0.33) with invariant lines near 1150, 1050 and 680 °C; this is a general thermodynamic calculation for the Fe–Be system rather than sample-specific data (block b0093, b0097, figure_019).
Rolled-state tensile properties of the 1.0Be alloy — YS 820.57 MPa, UST 1074.33 MPa, TE 30.71 % (Table 3) — pertain to the 1050 °C hot-rolled sample, not to the as-cast sample (block b0065, b0041).

Rolled-state microhardness of the 1.0Be steel — austenite 398.39 ±14.630 HV and ferrite 349.81 ±21.267 HV (Table 4) — pertains to the rolled sample, not the as-cast sample (which has austenite 475.80 HV and ferrite 437.40 HV) (block b0067, b0047).

Nominal composition of the as-cast 1.0Be sample (wt%): Fe balance, 30 Mn, 10 Al, 1.5 C, 1.0 Be (Table 1); Fe, Mn, Al, C are identical across all four Be levels and only Be differs (block b0015, b0018, b0019).

In the as-cast structure, a large number of spherical, rod-like or needle-like compounds appear due to beryllium addition and the Be–Fe phase forms 'ancient Chinese character' shaped precipitates at the austenite/ferrite boundary; these were reported for the as-cast Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe series including 1.0Be (block b0074, b0030).

The effect of Be on the rolled structure (conversion of the as-cast needle-like Be–Fe phase into spherical and dot-like precipitates after hot rolling, b0102, b0080) concerns the rolled state and is not a property of the as-cast sample.
